title: Why warm and helpful people may have fewer friends, according to psychology
description: Helping friends constantly, from airport pick-ups to providing emotional support, may be a cover for deep-rooted insecurities. Psychologists note this 'caretaker' behavior often arises from an association of worth with usefulness, acting as a defense to shield oneself from vulnerability. This dynamic can create superficial relationships where the helpers feel unappreciated and overly exhausted, ultimately leading to isolation despite their admirable generosity.
